wave.name: infrastructure
wave.goal: Loopflow reliably advances its own work and delivers verified releases. Infrastructure owns self-hosting reliability, releases, auth, execution continuity, exact control authority, and repository-wide architecture reduction. Recovery preserves work, human decisions, history, and assigned-worktree isolation; failures are bounded, truthful, and actionable. Public concepts and APIs remain legible, with one owner and truth source for each responsibility.

krs.text: You can ask a generic lf Session to do something, create a Task, and advance it without getting blocked by Loopflow’s plumbing.
You don’t have to track Sessions, remind agents to continue, or chase whether Tasks landed.

task.name: Account for scheduled release opportunities and settle actual release outcomes
task.description:
The bounded outcome is one authoritative connection between each due opportunity, its execution attempt, verification, and product result. It must distinguish published, no-change, deferred/resumable, and failed outcomes; account for wake delays and overlap without duplication; and demonstrate the two-settlement publication commitment.

Use existing release recovery and obligation-aware continuity code. Do not rebuild the scheduler or create a new release platform. If investigation reveals an independent publication blocker, name that blocker before splitting work. Keep at most one active Reliability implementation Task initially; this is a planning choice, not a runtime restriction.

The 35 failed telemetry targets remain counterevidence. A successful scheduler firing does not clear them, and required verification cannot be bypassed to obtain a publication receipt.

task.name: Keep published installation and main checkout updates reliable
task.description:
## Current contract — 2026-09-24

The human's global-cmds decision supersedes the combined refresh/package requirements in the original report below: `lf install` always updates the machine installation to the latest published Loopflow, independent of caller checkout; `lf rebase` owns checkout updates and preserves local work. Installation must not refresh main or run Homebrew/uv/developer dependency setup. Do not add `lf refresh` or a generic dependency-refresh framework. Keep the original main-rebase incident and its preservation proof obligations.

The global-cmds branch has candidate-level first-install/recovery fixes and removes the recursive Python refresh handoff. Review through ac0b51aad records 67 focused passes, plus three earlier checkout passes, and a disposable Ubuntu 24.04 candidate-package demo: no Git, fresh store, repeat without asset downloads, missing-daemon repair, unchanged dirty checkout and migration ledger, interrupted first-install recovery, and external installer transition from checksum-verified 0.12.18 binaries. That last account had no populated historical Home. Local HTTPS transport and materialized test migrations do not constitute a public-channel pass. Published 0.12.20 failed clean-home bootstrap in the recorded real demo. Real macOS app installation and populated historical Home migration remain unproven.

The accepted scheduling design is opt-in login plus weekly by default, with `lf install schedule [weekly|daily|hourly|5min]`: Monday 09:00, daily 09:00, on the hour, or clock multiples of five, in local time. Preserve the existing launchd label and custom LF_INSTALL_DIR, omit source WorkingDirectory/Python, and use calendar intervals. The concurrent scheduling receipt records a focused public-CLI cadence matrix and static checks, using simulated launchctl. A subsequent human clarification makes cadence positional (no --every flag); current source and design reflect that choice. Match final verification to those positional-argument bytes before acceptance. Preserve proof of defaults, each payload, cadence replacement, idempotence, unsupported values, and sleep/catch-up behavior at the appropriate fixture/configured boundary. Simulated launchctl does not prove a real login or wake event.

Keep this Task open. Remaining acceptance includes a released-path fresh install/repeat/repair, a real macOS complete-artifact check, the configured laptop path, and the original main/repeated-main/upstream-advances/preservation proofs. Retain the separate LOO-257 worktree-placement contract. This note records related branch evidence; it does not bind global-cmds to this Task, move its existing worktree/PR, start another worker, publish, or release. Branch ownership remains unresolved. Durable learnings live in wave/infrastructure/MEMORY.md.

## Original report — historical requirements superseded above

Make laptop refresh and lf rebase on main reliably catch up

Observed failure reported by the human on 2026-09-23: after going to the main checkout and running `lf rebase`, it failed with:

Error: rebase incomplete: pinned target bca3f35ac7d4ad24ebed2a30481d0b7ba3a86bde is not an ancestor of HEAD aef8c0c98a975a9bd3ceafc6bcedc3e2da37e408

Human intent: always be able to go to main and quickly create a new worktree from the latest main. Both of these are required:

1. Reliable automatic refreshing on the laptop as much as possible, including installing/updating the required packages and updating main.
2. `lf rebase` must work when invoked on main and mean catch up to the latest available upstream at invocation time, including any package/environment refresh that automatic refresh missed. Main is an ordinary supported context, not a branch to reject or a situation requiring manual git commands.

Restore the broken path, investigate the root cause, and implement durable prevention through the fix cycle. Inspect the actual configured laptop refresh/install mechanism and the main rebase path before deciding the change. Record the observed failure separately from hypotheses. Preserve caller edits and unpublished local commits while integrating upstream; do not solve this by destructive resets or publication. Missed automatic runs, laptop sleep, and transient fetch/install failures should recover on a later refresh or explicit invocation, with truthful actionable failures when an external dependency is unavailable.

Proof: reproduce the reported main-checkout failure where possible; prove that a stale main catches up through `lf rebase`, a second invocation works, and advancing upstream between invocations is picked up. Prove required package setup/update participates and that a missed or failed automatic refresh is caught up by explicit `lf rebase`. Demonstrate the configured laptop path and creation of a new sibling worktree based on the refreshed main using `lf`; label sandbox-only evidence honestly. A successful exit with stale main, a suppressed ancestry error, or only a feature-branch test does not count. Preserve normal feature-branch rebase behavior.

Related work: [LOO-257](https://linear.app/loopflow/issue/LOO-257/base-new-task-worktrees-on-current-canonical-main), Base new Task worktrees on current canonical main, is queued under Architecture Minimalism. Preserve its contract that clean local canonical main may contain unpublished commits and can be the base of a new Task worktree; do not impose origin equality or duplicate that task's placement redesign. This task owns refreshing main and the laptop environment.

task.name: Recover existing Tasks from Linear after installation state changes
task.description:
After updating the Loopflow binary, previously prepared and executing Etude Tasks disappeared from the default local view. The human wants a simple refresh/recovery path driven primarily by authoritative server-side Linear state, without manually finding old installation databases.

Observed 2026-09-24 (America/Los_Angeles):

* ETU-75 and ETU-79 existed in Linear with approved designs, existing Task worktrees, commits, and completed implement/compress/review-slice Runs.
* The updated installation local-198f5df536e545b7b63b3d15abeacdd2 selected its own \~/.lf-dev/installed/.../loopflow.db. lf task status returned "no Task exists" for both, and lf session list returned \[\].
* After the user restored Linear auth, doppler run -- lf pm sync succeeded and restored their planning definitions, but both showed runtime:null / "Task is ready to start". Existing execution identity and continuation were still invisible.
* Their intact records were found in prior installation local-afee63d734c7482cb94d1071af26d9ea. ETU-75 Task task_b08e8ed2768240ada6b3e3e4e65c0784; ETU-79 Task task_5f146d6379264c61a692b4eb58541637.
* Explicitly selecting that prior Home/store and its retained lf binary recovered exact Task/PR/worktree identities. Both prior finite slice flows had finished; resume correctly reported no active Flow. Selecting slice again launched implement Runs on the existing Tasks. No database rows were hand-edited or duplicate Tasks created.

Desired behavior:
An ordinary operator refresh/recover operation should use Linear as the primary authority for task definitions, scope, ownership and status, and reconcile them with available local execution evidence. It should explain missing local state, discover/adopt the exact existing Task/worktree/history where supportable, and expose a safe continuation instead of misleadingly suggesting the Task has never started.

Keep planning truth separate from process authority: Linear alone cannot prove a live worker, approved local-only gate, saved Flow position or merge. Preserve these when recoverable; report unknown or conflicting evidence with a specific recovery action. Never silently recreate a Task/worktree, overwrite edits, replay approval, infer completion, or start a second writer.

Acceptance:

* Reproduce an installation/store switch with an existing Task, retained worktree, completed and active/waiting Run variants.
* One supported refresh/recovery path restores correct visibility and safe resume from Linear plus retained local evidence; repetition is idempotent.
* Missing local history, changed Linear task metadata, terminal tasks, active workers and conflicting stores have truthful, actionable outcomes without duplicate execution.
* Preserve existing identities, commits, PR history and human decisions; make source/store selection visible enough to diagnose.
* Test the real installed CLI path, not only a database fixture.

Related: LOO-295 (Advance and repeated Task continuation), LOO-286 (lossless Task Flow cutover), and LOO-292 (laptop refresh/install reliability). This bug specifically owns post-installation state recovery from Linear and reconciliation of retained local Task execution. File only; the human has not requested launching implementation.

task.name: Restore Task continuation with a unified Advance action
task.description:
# Advance and Task continuation — LOO-295

Status: implementing and reviewing the authorized scope. Infrastructure owns this
Task in Loopflow. The User requested a new Task and direct execution here:
“implement -> compress -> review-slice to be clear”. No Task worker was launched.

## What to build

Make Advance accept an exact human review and drive a persisted Task Flow through
finite implementation/review Runs until human input, a blocker, or completion.

## Intent and placement

User anchors: “it doesnt seem to start what i expect which is some sort of
implement->review-slice with some way of indicating whether to terminate the loop
ro not”; “i think thats the lf task advance command basically”; “ok Advance”.
They also requested “an advance skill ... $advance in any codex session”.

Task: [LOO-295](https://linear.app/loopflow/issue/LOO-295). Wave: infrastructure.
This is an indivisible runtime change, implemented in internal slices and shipped
as one PR. Richer app progress presentation is a separate additive follow-up;
the Advance action label and command mirror belong here.

## Current system

v0.12.20 removed the first/loop/finally scheduler. `task-design` contains kickoff
and human review-design only. Completion deletes its FlowPosition. Separate
`slice` runs implement, compress, and review-slice once. The Task controller
settles one finite provider boundary, then launches another process. The store's
versioned claim fences writes; exact invocation/node/iteration tokens fence
human decisions. Session UI mirrors the CLI and owns no independent workflow.
These source facts explain the missing default continuation; we have not
reproduced the User's original Task in its live Home.

## Target architecture and data structures

The pinned Flow owns sequencing. `feature` composes `task-design` and `pursue`.
`pursue` repeats implement → compress → review-slice, then parks at human demo.
Default selection becomes feature; explicit selections and Project recommendations
remain authoritative. Already-pinned Flows do not silently acquire new steps.

`OccurrencePolicy.repeat: Option<RepeatPolicy { from, max_iterations }>` is a
backward edge on the autonomous reviewer. Its body contains autonomous skills;
no human gates, operations, or nested repeats. The initial limit is eight passes.
`FlowPosition.review: Option<LoopReview>` holds reviewer node identity, completed
passes, previous direction, and pending `ReviewVerdict { decision, summary }`.
Decision is Continue, Complete, or Blocked. No second Task phase/cursor is added.

`drive_task(store, task, claim, harness_factory)` repeatedly runs one boundary,
settles it, and claims the next. Each provider Run is fresh. The mechanical
process owns no model transcript and stops at human input, failure, interruption,
or flow completion. Existing claims prevent duplicate launches.

`record_review_verdict(task, run, verdict)` accepts only the currently claimed
reviewer and rejects conflicting duplicates. `finish_task_flow_turn` consumes
that evidence: Continue returns to the body and seeds its direction; Complete
enters final steps; Blocked, missing verdict, and exhaustion persist blockers.
Complete requires the whole approved design. Recovery can consume an already
saved verdict once; reported failure/interruption discards it. Flow completion
atomically records FlowFinished and removes the position. Work stays open.

## Public interaction and authority

`lf task advance ISSUE` drives the existing invocation or reports its wait.
`--session ID --summary TEXT` accepts an exact human gate before driving.
`lf session advance ID TEXT` is the Session action, replacing public Approve.
Internal approval remains an exact durable human decision. Iterate requests
revision. Readiness and ordinary agreement on one detail grant no approval.

A review prompt names its exact Advance command, tells the agent to save the
agreed artifact, and explains that explicit “go ahead” is sufficient. Settlement
and successor launch precede provider teardown. The terminal cradle reports the
resulting Task state after the review exits. Failed launches leave durable state
available for recovery, never an invented started receipt.

The advance skill resolves review, Task, or approved unbound design from the
conversation and repository. It preserves direct execution requests, checks
installed CLI capability, and reports actual status. Its canonical source ships
with Loopflow; a Codex SKILL.md is installed in the User's shared skills directory.

## Demo and Done when

Open a feature Task's design review, Advance, observe implementation without
selecting another Flow, request another slice through the typed review, then
observe final human demo once. A deliberately design-only Flow still finishes
at approval. Focused proof must cover fresh Runs across two passes, direction
carryover, durable finish, exact approval, competing/stale claims, interruption,
recorded-verdict recovery, missing/blocked/exhausted review, and schema retention.

The hermetic driver fixture runs the real controller/store with simulated
provider and Linear responses. Ghostty/provider transport and a live production
Home demo remain separate evidence; do not claim those from fixture results.
No merge or production installation is authorized by Advance alone.

## Constraints and forbidden outcomes

No resident provider, second first/loop/finally scheduler, recursive skill launch,
prose-parsed success, approval inferred from readiness, or compatibility command
alias. No failed exit counts as complete. A passing latest slice does not prove
the whole design. Repeat requires persisted Task execution; generic flows reject it.

## Internal slices

1. Completed: persisted repeat policy, verdict authority, migration, reducer.
2. Completed: mechanical driver, feature/pursue, CLI and app Advance, skill.
3. **This slice:** compress, behavioral review, recovery and integration proof.

Evidence and findings live in `scratch/review-slice.md`; that ledger supplements
this complete design. Follow-up intent: show readiness, next boundary, and loop
progress more richly in the app using these same durable facts.

task.description:
## Canvas integration amendment — 2026-09-24

The human's subsequent LOO-291 canvas direction supersedes the separate Watch/Changes/Terminal destination and independent nested split layout proposed below. Public navigation is one repo → Wave → Task → Session outline. Task Monitor, native Sessions and companion shells belong to the existing multiplexer, outer checkout slots and window-local surface pool. Adapt richer Watch content there; do not restore a Project tier, competing Task navigator or another pane tree.

Preserve this Task, implementation, checkout, passive output/Flow history and all remaining configured acceptance. LOO-291's initial Monitor lists only exact active Task Runs; that does not complete this Task or remove history, throughput/output or diagram work. Do not close LOO-293 merely because shared primitives now exist.

Consume required Session.run_id and shared Run/Work attribution. A prepared Run, unfinished manifest, active Flow stage, matching cwd or unresolved Session alone cannot prove liveness. The shared active-Run reader joins native receipts and exact generic capture intervals to verified process observations. Existing launchers' native receipts must remain discoverable without new markers. Its current retained-directory traversal remains unbounded and its UI uses demand refresh; do not claim bounded discovery or live polling from bounded payloads.

Keep active discovery, Flow history and passive output as independent reads with explicit gaps. Reuse the shared resolver and per-Run native readers instead of broadening Watch into planning/Session authority. Original headless Runs may later resume interactively: source selection based solely on original manifest.surface loses native output. Preserve original provenance and account/source/epoch identity while reconciling that path. Retained output limits must cover discovery and aggregate state, not only each page or Task.

Before acceptance, retain all-provider passive continuity, tool-result correlation, separate history/live paging, exact stage/attempt/return edges, auxiliary Runs, Follow live, stale/missing/reset evidence and the original configured human demo. Opening/closing observation must never launch, resume, transfer or interrupt a provider. Measure richer Monitor additions through LOO-291's Task workspace experience runner once its complete baseline exists; do not replace this Task's behavioral proof with synthetic DTO timing or current-active-only coverage.

The full earlier design and resolved-contract obligations follow as preserved history; only their conflicting presentation/identity assumptions are superseded. No new Task, live planning rotation, worker launch or completion occurs in this reconciliation.

---

## Preserved prior directive and evidence

# Restore Task watching with live session output and flow diagrams

## Accepted direction and execution

The human approved the attached draft in conversation and explicitly requested creating and advancing a Task, with the draft incorporated into the Task itself. This description embeds the complete draft and its open assumptions; it must remain sufficient after scratch is cleared.

Placement: Product wave, Desktop project. This resolves the draft's previously unresolved ownership. Build one end-to-end Task watcher, keeping live output and accurate stage diagrams together in one PR. Begin with the slice flow rather than repeating a kickoff conversation; retain the configured-path human demo gate before settlement.

Treat the native interactive transcript gap as required investigation and implementation within this Task, not permission to silently narrow the feature to autonomous Runs. Resolve the passive read contract in the Task design before dependent implementation. The accepted user-facing direction is Watch beside Changes and Terminal, a connected diagram of actual stages and attempts, one labeled feed across Task-attributed Runs, stage/Run filtering, Follow live, and inspectable completed history. Watching must never take over or interrupt an existing provider client.

Related work: LOO-291 joins Project/KR/Task planning to native Sessions. Consume its shared identities and navigation where available; this Task owns passive Task output watching and flow history, not a second planning or Session authority. Do not require that unrelated work to merge before investigating the watcher contract.

Implement and prove the complete design below, keeping current source/runtime differences explicit. Update the Task-local design as the native read contract is resolved. Do not claim all sessions are covered when an active supported interactive Session lacks passive output. Existing old Runs without retained evidence must show that limitation honestly.

## Resolved contract and remaining proof — 2026-09-23

This reconciliation supersedes draft-only API, placement, and implementation-status statements below while preserving the full accepted experience and pinned human/settlement gates. LOO-293 stays open under Product / Desktop; no remaining requirement is moved to a follow-up Task.

Committed foundation at 06ba29d57: Task-local events retain the immutable expanded invocation, exact stage/Run bindings, readiness/failure, Iterate/retry transitions, and settlement in the owning SQLite transactions. FlowPosition and its claim remain execution authority; inspection events never wake parent controllers. Passive native readers, launch/hook-owned source receipts, incremental output, file/stdin cursor transport, and the Rust/Swift output fixture are implemented. Concurrent Watch snapshot work is not validated by these foundation receipts.

Resolved passive contract: Rust reads Claude Session JSONL, Codex Session-matched rollout JSONL (including archived history), or exact OpenCode Session message/part rows through a read-only database. Resolve the recorded Session and exact account or the launch-owned native location stored in ProviderSessionRef; never select/refresh credentials, guess the observer's data root, or launch, resume, attach, replace, or interrupt the provider. Native records require source/item identity and revision beyond journal sequence numbers. TaskOutputPage groups ordered records and Run/provider/stage labels with availability/reset/gaps per TaskOutputSource. Normalize response items once, exclude event mirrors/internal instructions, and retain stable revisions for mutable parts. Source health belongs to output; missing plan/Run evidence belongs to the Watch snapshot.

The output command is `lf task output ISSUE --json [--cursor FILE]`; `--cursor -` reads stdin. Swift transports opaque values in a private temporary directory removed after success or failure. Input/output share a 4 MiB bound. OpenCode freezes the upper sweep timestamp and retains both inclusive boundary hashes and unfinished parts while paging; timestamp-only changes must not replay content. Partial JSONL tails wait; malformed/oversized complete records and resets remain explicit.

Remaining work in this same PR:

* Preserve native Claude/Codex call-result correlation through the shared shape and prove two same-tool calls returning out of order. Retain healthy Task output with explicit discovery uncertainty when unrelated manifests are malformed, missing, or disappear during reads. The concurrent foundation review reproduced both defects through synthetic CLI sources; repairs underway need their own focused proof.
* Complete autonomous/auxiliary tool-result capture (summary-only journals currently report limited_capture), faithful provider attribution across attempts, and configured Claude/OpenCode live proof. Prior Codex proof observed new prose/tools with the original owned client unchanged; it does not establish all-provider coverage.
* Separate historical paging from live continuation and bound discovery/retained state. Current discovery scans all manifests and flow facts on each query. Per-Run state, same-timestamp boundaries, and unfinished parts can hit the cap. Resolve or explicitly detect OpenCode backdated/equal-count completed-history rewrites; quiet output must not hide lost capture.
* Finish the shared Watch snapshot from one SQLite read transaction over position and ledger. Preserve expanded labels/ancestry, separate retries, exact return edges/settlement, active stage, auxiliary Runs, and explicit missing receipts. Do not fabricate a history cursor on an unpaged intermediate snapshot or mark interrupted/replaced attempts completed. Add Rust/Swift fixture and behavioral proofs.
* Finish Watch from Work, Roadmap, and Wave detail without worker/worktree prerequisites; filtering, Follow live across stages/Runs, older invocations/output, stale last-good evidence, accessible selection, visible-only polling/cancellation, and existing Session navigation.
* Prove autonomous and passive native output before completion, stage transition without reopening, previous-stage inspection then Follow live, concurrent auxiliary output, human Iterate with distinct attempts, and retained diagram/output after completion/reopen. Then enter the pinned configured human demo gate. Static diagrams, final-only output, terminal attachment, and autonomous-only coverage do not meet acceptance.

Prior file/stdin proof returned 469 distinct revisions and accepted a 2,186,420-byte padded cursor: transport capacity only, not realistic retained state or live arrival. Focused store/controller, native-reader, continuation, CLI/Swift transport, and DTO receipts are not a full Watch or release gate. Product / Desktop definitions and KRs do not change from this foundation.

## Incorporated draft design

# Task watcher

## What to build

Open any Task in the Mac app and watch its sessions' output arrive beneath a flow diagram that follows its actual progress, with earlier stages and attempts available to inspect.

User intent: “for any given task you were able to "watch" all the sessions output go by even as they were autonomous” and “we rendered flow charts for eac htask to show how it moved through stages.”

## Placement

Wave and Project unresolved: the seed names neither. This is a Task-level Mac visibility feature; no PM changes are needed to design it.

## Experience and demo

Add **Watch** beside **Changes** and **Terminal** in `TaskWorkspaceView`. Task entries in Work, Roadmap, and Wave detail expose the same Watch destination. Watching works without a live worker or surviving worktree. Changes and Terminal retain their existing prerequisites.

The upper pane shows the selected flow invocation as connected, selectable stage nodes. Show skill names, human checkpoints, operations, current state, and attempt counts. Group expanded steps by their existing flow ancestry. An Iterate transition draws a return edge to the stage actually revisited. Use text and icons as well as the existing status colors; support keyboard selection and reduced motion. Render the actual persisted plan, including custom flows; never hardcode the feature flow.

Below it, **All output** follows every Run attributed to the Task, including concurrent and auxiliary Runs. Label output with stage, Run, and provider; preserve each Run's event order and group contiguous output so parallel agents remain distinguishable. Auxiliary Runs stay visible without advancing the flow. Cross-Run ordering is observation order, not an assertion of causality.

Show streamed prose, commentary, commands, tool results, and failures. Long tool output can expand. A stage click filters to that stage's attempts; a Run click narrows further. Scrolling up suspends autoscroll. **Follow live** clears those filters and rejoins the live tail across stage and Run changes. An invocation selector exposes earlier flows after restart or serial PR work. Older output loads on demand.

Watch is read-only. Opening, closing, or reconnecting never resumes a provider, claims a Session, approves a checkpoint, or interrupts execution. A human checkpoint links to its existing interactive Session and decision controls.

Real demo: open Watch for a configured Task, see autonomous text and tool output, observe a stage finish and the next begin without reopening, inspect the previous stage, then follow live again. At a human checkpoint, open the existing Session and choose Iterate; see the recorded return path and separate attempts. Close and reopen after completion: the diagram and available transcript remain inspectable. Show a second concurrent Task Run in All output.

## Current system and evidence

Observed in this checkout, 2026-09-23:

* `TaskWorkspaceView.swift` offers Changes and Terminal and currently gates the entire workspace on runtime/worktree presence.
* `SessionRecord` represents interactive Sessions. Selecting one can launch/resume a native provider; it is not a passive autonomous output source.
* `session_command_status_with_env` in `lf/commands/util.rs` launches native clients with inherited terminal output and records client/session identity. The inspected path does not copy their conversation into Run events; the OpenCode observer extracts session identity only.
* `run_record.rs` stores sequenced, timestamped `events.jsonl`, including normalized conversation events, text/tool summaries, raw provider output, and outcomes. `RunSnapshot` has Task attribution and parent Run identity.
* `lf runs --task` silently limits discovery to seven days and approximately fifty Runs; `--events` reads one entire file. Neither contract supports complete, incremental Task watching.
* `FlowPosition` retains the expanded `QueuedInvocation`, cursor, iteration, and current worker/Session Run. Store mutations replace the cursor and delete the position on completion. `RunSnapshot` alone cannot identify historical stage occurrences.
* Historical commit `f56f457a0` (2026-02-08) added parsed live output and run history. At `c3bd1fdb3` (2026-03-30), `WaveDetailPanel` combined `LiveOutput` and `FlowProgressPills`. This is a close behavioral precedent, not confirmation of the exact remembered screen; the old surface was Wave-based.

## Data structures and ownership

Retain `FlowPosition` as execution authority and Run journals as output authority. Extend the existing Task event ledger with committed flow facts: invocation selected (expanded plan), stage entered, Run bound, decision/transition, and invocation settled or replaced. Write these in the same transactions as the corresponding position mutations, including human boundaries and completion. Keep these inspection facts local to the Task rather than triggering Project/Wave observations.

Identify stages by `(invocation_id, step_index)` and attempts by iteration plus Run identity. Bind from the owning transaction; never match by skill name or timing. The invocation's expanded plan is an immutable historical receipt, not another mutable flow definition.

Proposed read DTOs:

* `TaskWatchSnapshot`: Task identity, flow invocations/stages/transitions, attributed Runs, evidence availability, history cursor.
* `TaskOutputPage`: attributed output records, per-Run cursors, next history cursor, and explicit source gaps.
* Output identity: `(run_id, event_seq)`; retain turn/item identities for delta folding. Reuse existing conversation payloads where possible.

Every wire field is required or explicitly optional. Add Rust/Swift fixture coverage. Swift owns selection, folding, and scroll position; it owns no durable lifecycle state.

## Key functions and reads

Proposed commands: `lf task watch ISSUE --json` for the snapshot; `lf task output ISSUE --json [--cursor CURSOR]` for bounded incremental output and paginated history. These are read operations implemented over shared Run and Task readers, without the recent-Runs cap.

Proposed functions:

* Rust `read_task_watch(store, task_id) -> Result<TaskWatchSnapshot>`: join committed flow facts and attributed Runs.
* Rust `read_task_output(store, task_id, cursor) -> Result<TaskOutputPage>`: discover new Runs and read only complete new records, with bounded pages and opaque continuation.
* Swift `RegistryQuery.taskWatch(task:cwd:)` and `taskOutput(task:cursor:cwd:)`: typed CLI reads.
* Swift `TaskWatchStore.refresh()`: merge identities, fold deltas, retain selection and last-good evidence.

Poll while visible, initially once per second; cancel reads when hidden. Cursor state includes discovery progress and per-Run positions so new Runs join automatically. Incomplete trailing JSON waits for the next read; malformed complete records surface a gap. Reconnect deduplicates identities. Do not render normalized events and their raw provider copies twice. ## Data structures and key functions

### Optional conversations, one current at a time

User direction:

> “open a session with either the repo, wave, or proejct, but much like wiht a task you really only have 1 such session at a time, you only have the "one" session per level”

Each individual repo, Wave, Project, and Task offers an optional conversation, with at most one current user conversation at a time. Encourage bounded conversations and fresh starts. The durable subject persists independently of its conversations. The repo is a Session scope, not a new durable Work kind.

* Put Start conversation on the repo header, compact Wave/Project headings, and Task rows when no conversation is current. It starts fresh rather than automatically resuming the last historical conversation. Merely selecting a subject does not start a conversation.
* While a conversation is current, offer Continue and an explicit Start fresh. Continue returns to that exact conversation; Start fresh ends the prior ordinary conversation and begins a new one with fresh conversational context. Preserve prior history for deliberate access. Do not automatically replay old transcripts into fresh conversations.
* Finish conversation leaves the subject with no current conversation. It does not complete the Task, stop its autonomous work, remove its checkout, or close companion shells. A later Start conversation begins anew. Labels must distinguish conversation completion from Task completion.
* Repeated Continue actions across views/windows converge on the same Session identity. Starting fresh is an explicit lifecycle change, never a side effect of navigating. Client ownership still uses explicit Move here.
* The chosen Session can use A or D. Changing layout, hiding its view, or collapsing its parent does not finish it. Historical conversations are history rather than sibling current-session rows.
* Autonomous Runs remain independent execution evidence. Their presence does not consume or replace the subject's human Session.
* Repository-level exploration has a home before a Task exists. A repo Session can concern work in a checkout without that path becoming a Task or another hierarchy level. Do not infer Task ownership from cwd.

This supersedes the proposed standalone-Session/worktree inventory as the primary navigator. Do not add an “unfiled” queue or multiple current Session children under each subject. Worktrees own terminal grouping as designed in `lf-new`; they are not a fourth planning kind. Prefer that design's Task-first creation path for new implementation work. Existing unbound work still needs access and a non-destructive path into tracked work; do not silently create a second current repo conversation.

Existing Rust/Swift Session records already carry optional typed Work attribution, cwd, and stable Session identity; they do not yet establish this cardinality or a repo-session association. Shared start/continue/finish operations must own that relationship, not a Swift-only filter that hides extra live Sessions. Before implementation, reconcile existing multiple Sessions and Ask/FlowStep human boundaries: preserve pending decisions and history without silently closing, replacing, or hiding them. Optional conversation controls must not silently approve, iterate, or release a mandatory human boundary. Exact replacement/recovery semantics remain to be designed. No migration or API support is claimed by this sketch.

Next mockup: a repo Session, a Wave Session, a Project Session, and Task-owned autonomous/human work, all opened through their corresponding header/row. The separate Sessions-only window may become unnecessary once these paths have equivalent reachability.

### Existing shared values

Retain `RoadmapSnapshot`, `RoadmapTask`, `SessionRecord`, `WorkReference`, and `PodiumReading` as source values. `WorkspaceProjection` preserves Wave/Project nesting and each subject's optional current Session; a view-only `WorkspaceTask` carries one planning Task and its optional current Session. Its key uses repository plus planning Task id, so starting runtime does not change identity. Session identity remains stable independently of view placement. Expansion is a view-local set of typed node keys, separate from terminal layout and Work selection.

Proposed Swift seams:

* `projectWorkspace(roadmap: RoadmapSnapshot, sessions: [SessionRecord]) -> WorkspaceProjection`: associate by typed identity; retain unmatched Sessions explicitly.
* `selectWork(_ selection: WorkReference?)`: inspect without opening a provider.
* Proposed `startConversation(for: SessionTarget)`, `continueConversation(id:)`, and `finishConversation(id:)`: explicit shared lifecycle by repository or typed Work identity. Fresh replacement is a deliberate transition; exact backend API and recovery remain to be designed.
* Existing `SessionsStore.select(_:)`: open/focus the returned Session through its shared preparation path.

Planning Task ids and durable `runtime.workId` differ. Use the explicit shared relationship, never titles, branch names, or cwd guesses. Session identity remains its own id. Rust owns legal actions; Swift owns selection, filters, pane focus, and opening errors.

`PodiumView` switches between `.sessions` and `.work`. `WorkSurfaceView` uses `nowSections`, which omits clear conditions. `SessionsView` lists Sessions and separately reads the roadmap to enrich labels. `PodiumModel` already reads planning and Sessions. `SessionsWorkspaceRegistry` retains per-window/per-repository multiplexer and surfaces.

Replace the root switch and parallel navigation with the unified tree, including the competing cascading hierarchy in `PodiumConsole`. Reuse work inspectors and Activity. Integrate `lf-new`'s per-window/per-worktree surface ownership and outer worktree layout; do not retain repository-wide grouping as the target or implement a second workspace registry here.
